expectations.text: Creates a Markdown design doc under docs/design/ in the project
The document is written in Portuguese, matching the conversation language
expectations.evidence: Whole document in Portuguese: 'Visão geral', 'Escopo e contexto', 'Trade-offs da solução escolhida', 'Questões em aberto'.

expectations.text: The accepted trade-off — loss of immediate download for small exports — appears explicitly as a cost of the chosen solution
expectations.evidence: Trade-offs section: '✗ O usuário perde o download imediato. Exportações pequenas, que hoje funcionam na hora, passam a chegar por e-mail. O time aceitou esse custo em troca do caminho único.' Also stated in the solution overview.

expectations.text: Alternatives include the two discussed (longer synchronous timeout, external BI tool) and also 'do nothing'
expectations.evidence: Alternatives table rows: 'Não fazer nada', 'Gerar síncrono com timeout maior', 'Ferramenta de BI externa', and the chosen worker/fila/S3 path, each with cost and decision.

expectations.text: Cross-cutting concerns cover the platform team (shared queue) and the security team (signed links with PII)
expectations.evidence: 'Preocupações transversais' has subsections 'Plataforma (fila compartilhada)' and 'Segurança (link assinado com PII)'; both teams also listed as reviewers in the header.

expectations.text: A glossary is included or suggested at the beginning of the document covering terms a reviewer could stumble on (e.g. PII, BI, S3); it does NOT carry entries for universally known terms (API, HTTP, URL) nor for the document's own authoring tooling (C4, DSL, Structurizr)
expectations.evidence: Glossário right after the header: BI, Gateway, Job de exportação, Link assinado, PII, Streaming, Worker. No API/HTTP/URL, no C4/DSL/Structurizr/Mermaid entries. S3 is not glossed, but the assertion lists it as an example, not a requirement.

expectations.text: The architecture diagram is authored as Structurizr DSL and embedded as a Markdown image reference with the DSL folded inside a <details> block (rendered image when the structurizr tooling is reachable, placeholder otherwise); any flow diagram is a fenced ```mermaid sequence diagram; the architecture is never redrawn by hand in Mermaid
expectations.evidence: '![Diagrama de contêineres…](diagrams/Containers.svg)' followed by <details><summary>Fonte do diagrama (Structurizr DSL)</summary> with the workspace; Containers.svg exists (rendered via the -playwright image). Flow is a ```mermaid sequenceDiagram. Grader re-validated: structurizr validate exit 0, mermaid-cli exit 0.

expectations.text: Every diagram in the doc is followed by explanatory prose (no orphan diagrams)
expectations.evidence: C4 image followed by a bullet per container plus a paragraph on the gateway and the empty slots; sequence diagram followed by a step-by-step walkthrough (passos 1–3, 4–6, 7–9) and a happy-path-only note.

expectations.text: No invented facts: every metric in the doc traces to the prompt (30s timeout, 12% failures, 50k/100k rows); unknowns appear as open questions or explicit blanks, never fabricated values
expectations.evidence: Only 30 s, 12%, 50 mil and 100 mil appear. Link validity, retention, job payload, failure handling, volume are explicit open questions (10 listed); authors left as '(a preencher)'.

expectations.text: The overview section is at most two paragraphs and stays at solution-shape altitude: naming the core mechanism/technology is fine, but no schemas, payloads, endpoints, retry policies, or config values
expectations.evidence: 'Visão geral' is exactly two paragraphs naming RabbitMQ, worker, S3 and the e-mail link; no payloads, endpoints, retries or config.

expectations.text: No invented technology: every technology, protocol, datastore and product named in the document — including inside a diagram's DSL technology slots and relationship labels — traces to the prompt or to the repository; unstated ones are left blank and raised as questions
expectations.evidence: DSL technology slots: RabbitMQ and Amazon S3 only; API and worker have no technology; no relationship carries a protocol. 'Serviço de e-mail' draws the stated e-mail delivery with the sender left as open question 5. The doc says so explicitly under the diagram. Grader note: the DSL wires the worker as the e-mail trigger, a reasonable reading of 'quando termina' rather than an invented product.
